domain: International Relations Theory / Strategic Studies / Institutional History
topic_summary: Analysis of the post-1945 disappearance of winnable great-power total war from strategic planning space. The kernel question: did nuclear weapons make total war unwinnable (reading drop within reachable space) or remove it from consideration entirely (space contraction)? This tests whether commitment system structure can represent a reading becoming unreachable rather than merely disfavored.

key_entities: Nuclear weapons states (US, USSR, later UK/France/China)
Pre-1945 great power war planning apparatus (general staffs, mobilization doctrine)
Post-1945 deterrence theory establishment (RAND, strategic studies community)
MAD doctrine (Mutual Assured Destruction as stabilizing framework)
Limited war doctrine (Korea, Vietnam as constrained conflicts)
Non-nuclear rising powers (contemporary China, India as test cases)
key_tensions: Deterrence stability vs war-fighting capability (MAD vs counterforce)
Reachable-but-rejected vs unreachable (reading drop vs space contraction)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The strategic possibility space for great-power conflict resolution through total war
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Military planning establishments, strategic studies community, nuclear doctrine authorities

readings.commitment: Total war remains strategically reachable but is deterred by mutual vulnerability
readings.authority_grounding: MAD doctrine, arms control theory, rational deterrence models
readings.expected_structural_delta: War remains in planning space; constraint is cost-benefit calculation with extremely high costs. Generates continuous investment in war-fighting capability as deterrent signal. Reading predicts: doctrine development continues, counterforce targeting persists, escalation ladders remain theorized.

readings.commitment: Nuclear weapons removed total war from the strategically thinkable, not merely from the preferable
readings.authority_grounding: Constructivist IR theory, nuclear revolution thesis, epistemic community shift
readings.expected_structural_delta: War exits planning space entirely; constraint is categorical impossibility rather than high cost. Generates institutional atrophy of total-war planning apparatus. Reading predicts: mobilization doctrine disappears, general staff war-gaming for great-power conflict ceases, strategic studies shifts to sub-nuclear domains.

readings.commitment: Total war became normatively prohibited through constructed taboo, independent of material capability
readings.authority_grounding: Norm cascade theory, Tannenwald's nuclear taboo thesis, practice-based constructivism
readings.expected_structural_delta: War remains materially possible but normatively foreclosed. Generates norm-enforcement mechanisms (non-proliferation regime, no-first-use pledges). Reading predicts: taboo weakens if norm entrepreneurs exit, non-nuclear powers face different constraint structure.

axes.human_readable: Deterrence Equilibrium (Total War as Deterred but Reachable)
axes.structural_delta: Nuclear weapons raised costs of total war to mutual annihilation, making it strategically irrational but not impossible
axes.primary_observable: Continued investment in strategic nuclear forces, counterforce doctrine development, escalation control theory
axes.selection_reason: Dominant reading in strategic studies literature; generates distinct institutional predictions

axes.human_readable: Space Contraction (Total War as Categorically Unreachable)
axes.structural_delta: Nuclear weapons removed total war from strategic possibility space, not merely from preferred options
axes.primary_observable: Atrophy of mobilization doctrine, disappearance of total-war planning from general staff exercises, shift to limited-war focus
axes.selection_reason: Structurally distinct from deterrence reading; tests whether M-set can represent reading exit from reachable space

axes.human_readable: Nuclear Taboo (Total War as Normatively Prohibited)
axes.structural_delta: Total war became unthinkable through norm construction independent of material deterrence
axes.primary_observable: Non-proliferation regime strength, rhetorical treatment of nuclear use, norm-enforcement mechanisms
axes.selection_reason: Third structurally distinct reading; captures social construction dimension absent from material readings

axes.human_readable: Limited War Substitution (Proxy Conflicts as Constrained Outlet)
axes.structural_delta: Great powers shifted to limited wars and proxy conflicts as substitute for total war
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of proxy wars 1945-1991, explicit limitation doctrine (Korea, Vietnam)
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream consequence of deterrence reading rather than independent reading of kernel

axes.human_readable: Non-Nuclear Power Divergence (Rising Powers Face Different Constraint)
axes.structural_delta: Non-nuclear rising powers (pre-nuclear China, India) faced different strategic possibility space than nuclear states
axes.primary_observable: War planning doctrine in non-nuclear states, threshold at which nuclear acquisition changes doctrine
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: tests boundary conditions of readings but lower structural centrality than core readings

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Great powers shifted to limited wars as substitute for total war
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Downstream consequence of deterrence equilibrium reading rather than independent kernel reading

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Non-nuclear rising powers faced different strategic possibility space
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Tests boundary conditions but lower structural centrality; relevant for omega on reading universality

omegas.description: Does the M-set formalism have a cell for 'reading exits reachable space'? Space contraction reading claims total war became categorically unreachable, not merely deterred. If M-set has site-expansion but no contraction primitive, this reading may be inexpressible in current formalism. Library verdict context suggests this is the core test case.
omegas.source: User kernel contest flag + §1.3-K kernel recognition

omegas.description: Do deterrence and taboo readings collapse into one constraint? Both predict non-use, but deterrence predicts continued capability investment while taboo predicts norm-enforcement investment. If observables converge (e.g., both predict no great-power nuclear war), readings may be empirically indistinguishable despite different generative mechanisms.

Do these readings apply to non-nuclear rising powers? If China (pre-1964) or India (pre-1974) maintained total-war planning doctrine, space contraction reading is falsified for non-nuclear states. Deferred axis non_nuclear_power_divergence bounds this uncertainty.
omegas.source: Deferred axis non_nuclear_power_divergence + Dark Matter Probe 2

omegas.description: Does Russia's 2022 Ukraine invasion falsify space contraction reading? If great-power total war re-enters planning space (NATO-Russia escalation scenarios), contraction was temporary norm rather than structural impossibility. Deterrence reading predicts this as rational calculation; taboo reading predicts norm erosion; contraction reading has no mechanism for re-entry.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — contemporary great-power conflict absent from extraction

omegas.description: Model training on strategic studies literature may bias toward deterrence reading (dominant paradigm 1960-1990). Space contraction and taboo readings emerged later in constructivist IR. F34 risk: model may underweight non-rationalist readings due to training distribution.

Model training likely overweights rationalist deterrence literature (RAND, Schelling, Waltz) relative to constructivist norm theory (Tannenwald, Price, Finnemore).
